story_title: OpenAI Introduces GDPval to Benchmark Models on 44 Real-World Occupations
caption:
OpenAI just introduced GDPval—a new benchmark designed to measure model performance on real-world economically valuable tasks across 44 occupations.

Traditional benchmarks like MMLU or HumanEval test academic trivia or isolated code snippets. GDPval shifts the focus directly onto real workforce output.

What occupations do you think AI will master first? Drop your thoughts below.

alt_text_overall: Carousel explaining OpenAI's new GDPval benchmark, which measures AI model performance on real-world economically valuable tasks across 44 occupations.
alt_text_per_slide: Slide 1: 44 OCCUPATIONS. ONE NEW BENCHMARK.. OpenAI is changing how AI is evaluated—moving from abstract puzzles to real economic work. — shown as a bold statement over a torn-edge color block.

Slide 2: TRADITIONAL BENCHMARKS ARE FAILING.. Standard tests measure trivia, math, and isolated coding problems. They do not capture real daily jobs. — shown as a numbered slide beside a large offset circle.

Slide 3: INTRODUCING GDPVAL.. OpenAI introduced GDPval: a evaluation system explicitly designed to measure model performance on economically valuable tasks. — shown as a numbered slide beside a large offset circle.

Slide 4: TESTING ACROSS 44 OCCUPATIONS.. Rather than synthetic questions, GDPval measures performance across tasks spanning 44 distinct professions. — shown as a numbered slide beside a large offset circle.

Slide 5: FROM TRIVIA TO ECONOMIC VALUE.. Measuring model capability is no longer about academic scores. It is about workforce substitution and productivity. — shown as a numbered slide beside a large offset circle.

Slide 6: WHAT THIS MEANS FOR WORKERS.. When benchmarks track economic tasks directly, model updates will correlate to capability in specific jobs. — shown as a numbered slide beside a large offset circle.

Slide 7: THE ERA OF REAL-WORLD AI TESTING HAS ARRIVED.. The true benchmark of artificial intelligence is no longer what it knows, but what work it can perform. — shown as a bold statement over a torn-edge color block.
